title: Will Sara Duterte finally attend her impeachment trial?
summary: Vice President Sara Duterte says she had repeatedly told her defense lawyer, Michael Poa, 'Allow me to lawyer for myself and stand there as a lawyer'

blocks.text: YEAREND PRESSCON. Vice President Sara Duterte answers questions from the media during the Office of the Vice President's thanksgiving event in Mandaluyong City on November 27, 2026.
Jire Carreon/Rappler
Vice President Sara Duterte says she had repeatedly told her defense lawyer, Michael Poa, 'Allow me to lawyer for myself and stand there as a lawyer'
Will Vice President Sara Duterte ever show up at her impeachment trial?
That question has persisted since Day 1 of the trial on July 6, amid mounting calls for the Vice President to appear in court and personally respond to the allegations against her.

Duterte has visited the Senate on at least two occasions outside her trial. The first was on July 7, when she met with her defense team and delivered a one-sentence statement to the media, “In this bloodbath and bludgeoning, I will be bloodied but unbowed.”
She left the Senate before the trial could resume.
On November 26, Duterte returned to the chamber while the trial was suspended to attend plenary deliberations on her office’s proposed P785.2 million budget for 2027.

She exchanged pleasantries with some of the senators serving as judges in her trial. But when the media asked questions, including whether she will attend her trial, she only responded with “Merry Christmas.”
Duterte’s defense team has repeatedly said her attendance would depend on how the trial unfolds, stressing that her physical appearance is not required because she is fully represented by counsel.
Duterte herself said in August that the participation of her lawyers was “sufficient” and tantamount to her attending the impeachment proceedings.

But in a rare, nearly hour-long press conference at the Office of the Vice President central office in Mandaluyong City on Friday, November 27, Duterte claimed that she had long wanted to attend her trial. It could be recalled that the Vice President herself had repeatedly questioned the impeachment proceeding itself, describing it as “political theater” in the guise of accountability.
On Friday, Duterte said that her defense lawyer and former spokesperson, Michael Poa, ignored her whenever she raised the possibility of her appearance at her trial.

“Ilang beses na ako nagsabi sa kanya: ‘Michael Poa, allow me to enter my appearance for myself. Allow me to lawyer for myself and stand there as a lawyer.’ Hindi niya talaga ako pinapansin at all. Somehow, nililihis niya ‘yung usapan,” Duterte said at her latest press conference.

(I’ve told him several times, “Michael Poa, allow me to enter my appearance for myself. Allow me to represent myself and stand there as a lawyer.” He really didn’t pay attention to me at all. Somehow, he keeps steering the conversation away from the subject.)
Poa, defense spokesperson, has yet to respond to requests for comment.

Asked whether she could still be presented as a witness at this point, with the defense nearing the end of its presentation, Duterte said she had yet to discuss the matter with her lawyers. “We are not there yet but sabi kasi nila tapos na sila this week e. So hindi pa namin napag-uusapan kung a-attend ako as witness o hindi,” Duterte said.
(We are not there yet but they said they will be done this week. So we have not discussed yet if I will attend as a witness or not.)

The defense team is set to present two witnesses when the trial resumes next week. Both are expected to testify in relation to Cale88 Foods Corporation, a company at the center of allegations of unexplained wealth against Duterte.

Will Duterte at least be present when the impeachment court hands down its decision? The court targets a ruling by December 18. The Vice President indicated that this event, which her political fate hinges on, is not a priority.
“If I’m in Davao, then no. Because we have a series of activities for Davao thanksgiving for December,” she said in response.

Duterte also said her office is “preparing for the worst” and that she would accept the court’s decision. However, she cautioned that removing an elected vice president would have “consequences,” pointing to possible negative public reaction.

blocks.caption: Will Sara Duterte finally attend her impeachment trial?

blocks.text: Meanwhile, the Vice President said she would not fly to The Hague for the trial of former president Rodrigo Duterte for a crimes against humanity case before the International Criminal Court beginning November 30. She said it would be a “waste of money” as visits to her father would not be allowed during the trial.

She shared that she owed friends at least P5 million which helped cover for her trip to The Hague last year, as well as legal expenses for her impeachment trial and her father’s case. She said she planned to sell properties to repay her debt.

Duterte is facing one remaining allegation in her impeachment case: unexplained wealth. The House prosecution panel dropped the three other articles of impeachment, which involved grave threats, misuse of confidential funds, and bribery. – Rappler.com
